### 1. Parabola Construction (Focus-Directrix Method)
1. Draw a vertical line representing the directrix ($DD'$).
2. Draw a horizontal axis line perpendicular to $DD'$ passing through the midpoint.
3. Mark the focus ($F$) at a distance of $60\text{ mm}$ from the directrix on the axis line.
4. Mark the vertex ($V$) at the midpoint of $FF'$ ($30\text{ mm}$ from the directrix).
5. Mark several points $1, 2, 3, \dots$ along the axis beyond $V$.
6. Erect vertical lines through these points. With centre $F$ and radius equal to the distance from directrix to points $1, 2, 3$, cut arcs on the respective vertical lines above and below the axis.
7. Join the intersection points smoothly with a curve to complete the parabola.

### 2. Tangent and Normal at $80\text{ mm}$ from Directrix
1. Measure $80\text{ mm}$ from the directrix along the axis (or use coordinates) to locate the point $P$ on the curve.
2. Join point $P$ to the focus $F$.
3. Draw a line through $F$ perpendicular to $PF$ meeting the directrix at point $T$.
4. Join $T$ and $P$ and extend it to get the **Tangent** line.
5. Draw a line perpendicular to the tangent passing through $P$ to get the **Normal** line.
proTip: Ensure the normal is strictly perpendicular to the tangent at the specific point $P$.
